source_user: Choose between tensor and pipeline parallelism for a latency-sensitive multi-GPU service. State the assumptions needed. Scenario variant 147: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: compare per-GPU memory, communication topology, layer partitioning, batch and microbatch behavior, synchronization, latency target, and failure/reconfiguration costs.
corrected_answer: Scenario variant 147: Choose only after measurement; do not invent platform facts. Assume fixed model/checkpoint, precision, GPU count/type and usable memory (GiB), placement and interconnect, software/clock policy, request prompt/output distributions, arrival rate, concurrency, batching, and explicit p50/p95/p99 end-to-end, TTFT, and TPOT targets in ms. Define throughput/goodput units and quality, error-rate, availability, and memory-headroom gates. Pre-register the falsifiable hypothesis that, at the specified load and gates, the selected feasible configuration lowers held-out p99 by at least a pre-set M ms or M% versus the best feasible alternative; otherwise report inconclusive. Enumerate feasible tensor-parallel degrees and pipeline layer partitions. Measure TP shard memory, collective bytes/time, topology, synchronization, and stragglers; measure PP stage balance, activation memory/transfers, microbatch count, pipeline bubbles, queueing, and reconfiguration time. Run randomized repeated paired trials on isolated equivalent hardware with identical traces, warm-up, seeds, and versions; separate tuning from held-out evaluation and stratify by prompt/output length and load. Report units, confidence intervals, per-request tails, utilization, memory headroom, quality, failures, and recovery. Treat topology, kernel behavior, overlap, batching, and fault behavior as confounders unless measured. Test only authorized isolated failure/reconfiguration scenarios, protect production and data, and define rollback to the last known-good configuration on p99, quality, error-rate, availability, or memory-gate violation. Evidence required: versioned configs, topology and memory telemetry, synchronized traces, trial logs, correctness/quality checks, failure/recovery logs, and held-out results.
